items.body: EDITION Türkçe English BHSC Pусский Français العربية Kurdî کوردی Shqip فارسی македонски Bahasa Indonesia Español US-Iran war Hormuz crisis Russia-Ukraine war World Morning Briefing: Nov. 8, 2026 Anadolu’s recap of top stories from around the globe Esra Tekin 08 November 2026 • Update : 08 November 2026 ISTANBUL Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start Sunday, including Poland's interior minister's claim that far-right ideologies may have influenced a Krakow attacker; Israeli President Isaac Herzog's appointment of Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government; and the US army's announcement of a new task force to disrupt Iran's supply routes. Initial indications suggest that the suspect who opened fire in central Krakow, Poland's second-largest city, was influenced by far-right ideologies, according to Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski. Kierwinski told a news conference that police opened fire on the suspect three minutes after receiving the first report of the attack. He confirmed that six people were killed, including one foreign national, while 16 were injured, including five foreign nationals, two police officers and the suspect. Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced that he will task Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government, Israeli news site Ynet reported. Eisenkot has been invited to receive the mandate at a ceremony at the President’s Residence on Sunday at 5 pm local time (1500GMT), according to the report. Once he receives the mandate, Eisenkot will have 28 days to form a government. Herzog can grant an extension of up to 14 days under Israel’s Basic Law. The US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the establishment of a new task force aimed at disrupting Iran’s use of land routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials, expanding Washington’s pressure on Tehran. In a statement on US social media platform X, CENTCOM said Adm. Brad Cooper, the command’s chief, directed the formation of Task Force Iron Gate on Nov. 7. The unit, comprising approximately 20 civilian and military personnel, will be based in Tampa, Florida. The task force will work with other US government agencies to monitor and prevent the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and what Washington describes as illegal revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea. items.headline: France's fourth weekend of protests draws 146,000
items.summary: the interior ministry counted 46,000 in Paris, with clashes despite a lower turnout than previous weeks.
items.matters: five months from a presidential vote the far right sees as its best chance.
items.body: PARIS: Thousands of people protested across France Saturday in a new show of anger against the government with clashes erupting between police and some protesters in Paris despite a lower turnout than on previous weeks. The protests marked the fourth consecutive weekend of demonstrations against the rising cost of living which have erupted as the country heads to presidential elections in five months' time where the far right sees its best chance yet to win power. A total of 146,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Saturday, including 46,000 in Paris, the interior ministry said. Unions put the figure at 250,000 protesters nationwide, with 75,000 in the capital. These figures were lower than the previous three weekends of protests but also came after a mass union protest on Thursday that rallied 575,000 people according to the authorities – 1.6 million according to unions. At the end of the protest in Paris, police used tear gas against individuals throwing projectiles and homemade fireworks at the security forces, an AFP correspondent said. Police said a group of 200 violent individuals attacked officers as they were arresting a man who had set fire to a trash bin in the square. Some 70,000 members of the security forces were deployed Saturday, ready to move in quickly after mass protests on Oct 17 degenerated into the worst riots seen in France in years. Unions had staged a march along a traditional route, from the Place de la Republique in central Paris to Place de la Nation in the east of the city where the clashes erupted at the end of the protest. But the Yellow Vests movement – a group whose protests shook Emmanuel Macron in the early years of his presidency almost a decade ago – called for a rival demonstration at the Place de la Concorde in central Paris, a stone's throw from the president's Elysee Palace and the lower house of parliament. This action has been banned by the authorities, and on Saturday a large police presence prevented protesters from getting close. Some 100 people who arrived were surrounded by police and one of the movement's coordinators, Benjamin Ball, and its spokeswoman, Azelma Sigaux, were among those arrested by police, an AFP reporter said. In the southeastern city of Lyon, police fired tear gas to disperse several hundred people in the city centre blocking a road during an unauthorised gathering. The wave of demonstrations was sparked by a movement in late September by high school students angered by conditions at their establishments. These teens, joined by university students, remain at the heart…

items.headline: Strzelanina na Rynku Głównym w Krakowie
items.summary: zamaskowany 24-latek wjechał samochodem na Rynek i otworzył ogień do przechodniów; zginęło sześć osób, 16 zostało rannych, w tym dwaj policjanci.
items.matters: Tusk nazwał to zamachem i przyznał, że Polska nie miała dotąd tak drastycznego przypadku terroryzmu.
items.body: Sześć osób zginęło, 16 jest rannych po strzelaninie na Rynku Głównym w Krakowie. Sprawca, 24-latek, został zatrzymany. Polityka Strzelanina na Rynku Głównym w Krakowie. Relacja minuta po minucie W sobotę tuż po godz. 15 zamaskowany 24-latek wjechał autem na Rynek Główny w Krakowie i otworzył ogień do ludzi. Zginęło sześć osób, kilkanaście j... Jak wynika z relacji świadków i informacji służb, tuż po godz. 15 na płytę Rynku Głównego wjechał z impetem samochód. W środku siedział zamaskowany mężczyzna, który zaczął strzelać z broni palnej do przechodniów. Wystraszeni ludzie rzucili się do ucieczki i chowali się w pobliskich kawiarniach, restauracjach oraz bramach kamienic. Magistrat ustalił również, że z przejeżdżającego auta ostrzelano tramwaj linii nr 1. Szyba w kabinie motorniczego została rozbita, ale ani pasażerowie, ani prowadzący skład nie ucierpieli. Fotoreporter współpracujący z PAP relacjonuje, że napastnik uciekał przed policją, a na skrzyżowaniu z ul. Dietla zderzył się z białym autem. Wtedy wysiadł z pojazdu i otworzył ogień w stronę funkcjonariuszy. Rzeczniczka Komendy Wojewódzkiej Policji w Krakowie podinsp. Katarzyna Cisło przekazała, że policjanci odpowiedzieli strzałami, postrzelili napastnika i go obezwładnili. Premier Donald Tusk poinformował po odprawie z szefami służb, że w domu sprawcy odkryto zwłoki trzech osób: dwóch kobiet i mężczyzny. – Wiele wskazuje na to, że to najbliżsi członkowie jego rodziny – powiedział szef rządu. Wieczorem rzecznik KGP podinsp. Andrzej Fijołek przekazał PAP, że ciała znalezione w mieszkaniu w Ostrowcu Świętokrzyskim należą najprawdopodobniej do rodziców i siostry zamachowca. Zastrzegł, że oficjalne potwierdzenie będzie możliwe dopiero po zakończeniu czynności służb. Policja ze Świętokrzyskiego potwierdziła natrafienie na trzy ciała podczas działań w Ostrowcu Świętokrzyskim, gdzie funkcjonariusze przeszukują dom 24-latka. Asp. szt. Artur Majchrzak z zespołu prasowego KWP w Kielcach zaznaczył, że czynności wciąż trwają, a okoliczności śmierci tych osób nie zostały jeszcze wyjaśnione. Przestępczość Donald Tusk: W domu napastnika z Krakowa znaleziono ciała trzech osób W domu 24-letniego sprawcy sobotniego ataku w Krakowie znajdują się ciała dwóch kobiet i mężczyzny – poinformował podczas briefingu premier Donald... Szef MSWiA Marcin Kierwiński powiedział na konferencji w Małopolskim Urzędzie Wojewódzkim w Krakowie, że policjanci oddali pierwsze strzały do napastnika trzy minuty po zgłoszeniu. – Błyskawiczna reakcja policjantów uchroniła nas przed znacznie większą masakrą. (...) Straż pożarna i pogotowie…

items.headline: Bohaterowie z Krakowa: Kulik i Morański
items.summary: Tusk ujawnił nazwiska policjantów, którzy zatrzymali zamachowca; obaj są w stanie ciężkim po operacjach.
items.matters: brygada powietrznodesantowa apeluje o oddawanie krwi dla jednego z funkcjonariuszy.
items.body: 8 listopada 2026, 05:32 282 komentarze Udostępnij Udostępnij na Facebooku Udostępnij na X Udostępnij na WhatsApp Kopiuj link Działo się w nocy Źródło zdjęć: © PAP | PAP/Piotr Polak W nocy z soboty na niedzielę spływały kolejne informacje dotyczące zamachu w Krakowie. Premier Donald Tusk podał nazwiska bohaterskich policjantów, którzy powstrzymali zamachowca. Brygada Powietrznodesantowa zaapelowała o oddawanie krwi dla jednego z tych funkcjonariuszy. Z kolei w związku z zamachem Jarosław Kaczyński zaapelował o odwołanie manifestacji przeciwko działaniom rządu w sprawie Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Zapraszamy na skrót wydarzeń z nocy, czyli najważniejsze i najciekawsze materiały wybrane przez redakcję Wirtualnej Polski. Znajdziesz go codziennie o 6.30 na stronie głównej WP. Premier Donald Tusk odniósł się do stanu zdrowia funkcjonariuszy, którzy brali bezpośredni udział w zatrzymaniu 24-letniego zamachowca w Krakowie. Szef rządu postanowił oficjalnie wymienić ich z nazwiska, dziękując za heroiczną postawę. DLA CIEBIE Sąsiedzi zamachowca z Krakowa są w szoku. Tak o nim mówią "Starszy posterunkowy Jakub Kulik i starszy posterunkowy Artur Morański to prawdziwi bohaterowie. Uratowali prawdopodobnie wiele ludzkich istnień, nie zważając na ryzyko utraty życia ". – napisał Donald Tusk w mediach społecznościowych. "Ich stan jest poważny, ale są pod bardzo dobrą opieką. Cała Polska trzyma za Was kciuki " – dodał szef rządu we wpisie. Premier ujawnił nazwiska rannych policjantów. "Cała Polska trzyma kciuki" Bohaterska postawa policjantów. Apel o krew Brygada Powietrznodesantowa im. gen. Sosabowskiego zaapelowała o oddawanie krwi dla policjanta, który został ciężko ranny podczas sobotniej strzelaniny w Krakowie. W sobotę odniósł ciężkie obrażenia podczas wymiany ognia z zamachowcem w Krakowie. "Jakub jest bohaterem, który ratował innych, a teraz to on potrzebuje wsparcia. Potrzebna jest krew grupy AB Rh+. items.headline: Sejm uchwalił ustawę o środkach ograniczających
items.summary: za przyjęciem "konstytucji sankcyjnej" głosowało 240 posłów, 202 było przeciw; minister spraw wewnętrznych będzie mógł wpisać na listę sankcyjną decyzją administracyjną.
items.matters: przepisy wykonują prawo UE, ale opozycja ostrzega przed sankcjami bez wyroku sądu.
items.body: "Zagłosowałem za ustawą o środkach ograniczających. To był mój błąd (...) Przepraszam za ten głos" - napisał Marcin Józefaciuk. Były poseł KO zapowiedział, że zwróci się do Karola Nawrockiego z apelem o zawetowanie projektu, który został w piątek uchwalony przez Sejm. Sejm uchwalił w piątek ustawę, której celem jest utworzenie systemu krajowych środków ograniczających , w tym wprowadzenie nowych przesłanek pozwalających na wpis na listę sankcyjną. Według autorów ustawy, nowe przepisy mają stanowić "konstytucję sankcyjną" zawierającą ramowe uregulowania prawne, do których mogą się odnosić zarówno organy administracji publicznej, jak i podmioty prywatne. Jednym z posłów, którzy opowiedzieli się za ustawą był Marcin Józefaciuk , o czym poinformował w mediach społecznościowych. Dodał jednakowoż, że głos oddał przez pomyłkę. "Źle umieściłem ten punkt we własnym scenariuszu głosowań. W trakcie intensywnej serii głosowań nie wychwyciłem pomyłki . To ja odpowiadam za oddany głos" - napisał. Polityk przypomniał, że zgłaszał zastrzeżenia "do gwarancji prawa do obrony i kontroli sądowej" i zamierzał "zagłosować przeciw ustawie w tym brzmieniu". Ostatecznie przyczynił się do jej uchwalenia. "To był mój błąd" - nie krył Józefaciuk. "Będę dokładniej przygotowywał scenariusze głosowań . Jeśli ta ustawa wróci do Sejmu, tuż przed oddaniem głosu jeszcze raz sprawdzę, nad jakim rozwiązaniem dokładnie głosujemy i czy zapisana decyzja jest zgodna z moim stanowiskiem. Przepraszam za ten głos" - napisał, dodając, że zwróci się do Karola Nawrockiego z apelem o zawetowanie ustawy o środkach ograniczających. Projekt ustawy o środkach ograniczających została złożona w Sejmie przez rząd i ma na celu wykonanie prawa Unii Europejskiej. Za uchwaleniem ustawy wraz z dwoma doprecyzowującymi poprawkami głosowało 240 posłów, 202 było przeciwnych, 1 osoba wstrzymała się od głosu . Sejm głosował zgodnie z rekomendacjami połączonych komisji administracji, finansów publicznych oraz gospodarki, aby odrzucić wniosek o odrzucenie ustawy, przyjąć dwie poprawki o charakterze redakcyjnym i technicznym, a resztę poprawek odrzucić. Wśród nowych przesłanek pozwalających na wpis na listę sankcyjną znajdzie się m.in. ingerencja i manipulacja informacjami wymierzonymi w bezpieczeństwo narodowe. Ustawa określa też kary za naruszanie i obchodzenie sankcji . Ustawa określa w szczególności rodzaje i zakres zastosowania środków ograniczających, podział kompetencji między organami właściwymi, a także zasady odpowiedzialności związane z nieprzestrzeganiem nałożonych ograniczeń. Przepisy ustanawiają też m.in.…

items.headline: Thursday's AI rout set the week's tone
items.summary: the Nasdaq fell 5.5%, its biggest one-day point drop, on fears the Democratic sweep will slow data-centre construction.
items.matters: the index is in correction, more than 10% off its October high.
items.body: The stock market tanked on Thursday amid concerns that a shift in congressional political control following the U.S. midterm elections could slow the construction of data centers that power artificial intelligence services. Stocks sank across the board, but technology companies with a hand in the AI sector were hit especially hard. The Nasdaq Composite Index tumbled 1,422 points, or 5.5%, to close at 24,315. The drop means the tech-heavy index is now in a "correction," or down more than 10% from its most recent all-time high, set in October. The broader S&P 500 dropped 335 points, or 4.4%, to end at 7,354, while the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 1,833 points, or 3.4%. The decline continued on markets in Europe and Asia on Friday but U.S. shares were set to trade mixed. Dow futures were down 0.8% at 51,192.00. S&P 500 futures gained ground, adding almost 0.3% to 7,402.50. Market watchers think the Democrats' sweeping electoral victories this week could bolster opponents of data centers and slow the rollout of the facilities, which have spurred widespread public opposition. Investors are reacting to the growing "headline" risks around AI, according to Wall Street analyst Adam Crisafulli of Vital Knowledge. The rout was violent enough to potentially delay the highly anticipated initial public offering by Anthropic , a bellwether for the entire AI business, Crisafulli told investors in a research note. Before the turmoil in financial markets, the IPO had been expected to take place this month and to raise as much as $100 billion. The sharp drop also marks a sharp reversal from Wednesday, when the Dow posted its biggest gain of the year. Other indexes also surged after the election results eased uncertainty about who will control Washington. "Even though the market rallied Wednesday after the midterm elections, there were visible cracks in the AI ecosystem, and they widened on Thursday amid investor concerns about a potentially slower data center buildout with Democrats in charge of Congress," Chris Larkin, a managing director of trading and investing for E*TRADE from Morgan Stanley, said in an email. A slowdown in erecting data centers could deal a major blow to AI companies, which are pouring billions into the buildout and banking on widespread adoption of the technology. "The trigger for these moves appears to be the concern that the Democrats, both in Congress and at the state level, will seek to regulate the AI industry and restrict data center development," Joe Maher, markets economist with investment adviser Capital Economics, said in…

items.headline: Brent settles at $98.32 but loses 17% on the week
items.summary: the steepest weekly fall since the start of the pandemic, as traders priced in a possible US-Iran deal even while tankers kept burning.
items.matters: the war premium is unwinding faster than the war is ending.
items.body: HOUSTON, Nov 6 (Reuters) - Crude futures edged up late on Friday on renewed fears of further US strikes on Iran as US President Donald Trump said he would soon decide ‌whether to pursue a peace agreement or destroy what remains of Iran. Brent crude futures for January settled ‌at $98.32 a barrel, up 3 cents, or 0.03%. US West Texas Intermediate futures finished at $90.83 a barrel, up 31 cents, or 0.34%. The Brent ​contract is on track for a 17% decline this week, which would be its steepest weekly percentage fall since the start of the COVID pandemic and its biggest in absolute terms, according to LSEG data dating back to 1988. "A bit of unwinding of the war premium seems to be what's going on," said Phil Flynn, ‌senior analyst with Price Futures Group. In oil markets, signs of an emerging supply excess amid demand destruction were reinforced by spot premiums for Middle Eastern crude benchmarks returning to levels reached before the conflict. "The crude market is ​loosening to ​a state of oversupply based on the balance, but the ​quality difference still exists as refiners recover what ‌they can take versus what is available," said Rystad oil market analyst Janiv Shah, pointing to longer shipping routes and the need for ship-to-ship transfers as workarounds near the Strait of Hormuz. "The market is still looking for evidence of a firm deal being signed (on Iran), or any backlash from either party could tighten fundamentals once more." Also affecting futures was the strong jobs report issued by the US Department of Labor on Friday, showing an increase of 165,000 ‌jobs last month. "We're worried about the Federal Reserve raising interest rates ​after the jobs report this morning," said John Kilduff, partner with Again ​Capital. Oil prices fell 8% on Wednesday alone after ​the Democrats swept the US midterm elections, settling at two-month lows. However, prices rebounded on a ‌surge in tanker attacks in the Gulf and the ​Strait of Hormuz, renewing concerns ​over supply flows from the region. W ostatnich tygodniach obserwujemy coraz gorsze zachowanie złotego i polskich papierów skarbowych na tle regionu, ale rynek akcji do ostatniego piątku radził sobie doskonale. Sądy i trybunały Konflikt o Trybunał Konstytucyjny krok po kroku. Ściąga dla laika Zaczęło się w 2015 r.. Od tamtej pory sytuacja wokół Trybunału Konstytucyjnego się tak skomplikowała, że nawet wnikliwym obserwatorom trudno rozwik... items.headline: OpenAI closes $11bn at a $1.25 trillion valuation

items.body: OpenAI closes major funding tranche. OpenAI has completed the first portion of a new funding round, securing roughly $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, according to Bloomberg and Reuters citing people familiar with the matter. The funds were wired as of Friday. The full round could reach about $20 billion in coming weeks, well below the company’s earlier $30 billion target at a higher valuation, as public-market sentiment toward AI cooled. Investors in the initial close reportedly include SoftBank, Coatue, T. Rowe Price and others. OpenAI declined to comment. The raise comes amid broader market pressure and the company’s recent cybersecurity model work. Independent testers say Anthropic’s progress has roughly doubled. Nonprofit evaluator METR published an assessment finding that Anthropic’s models have been improving capabilities on well-specified tasks about 1.9 times faster since October 2025 than in the prior period, packing roughly two years of earlier progress into one. METR estimates that around 80 percent of the speedup comes from AI assisting the company’s own research and development rather than extra compute, based on internal data and staff interviews during an 11-week review. The group noted high uncertainty and that Anthropic redacted key evidence; the finding adds weight to discussions about AI accelerating its own advance. AI system helps close long-open quantum conjecture. Research organization PSI reported that an internal system running non-public Anthropic model instances produced a complete proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, open since 2008, by the third day of a run. The Lean proof assistant accepted it, and the system later improved the result. The conjecture concerns limits on quantum speedups for certain random problems. Verification so far rests on the formal Lean check plus an internal advisor audit; there is no peer-reviewed journal publication yet. Human researchers scoped the problem, reviewed the draft and take responsibility for correctness. Google lengthens and cheapens AI video generation. Google made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available, supporting video clips up to 15 seconds (up from 10) with multi-turn conversational editing, reference images and audio. Pricing falls about 30 percent to $0.07 per second for 720p, according to the company. It is offered via the Gemini API, AI Studio, Cloud and the app for higher-tier users, increasing pressure on rival video tools. Major labs back shared cyber-jailbreak rating system. The Frontier Model Forum, whose members include OpenAI, Anthropic, Google…

items.body: METR’s 5 November assessment estimates that Anthropic’s AECI benchmark scores have improved at 1.9 times their pre-October 2025 rate, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.5–2.8 times. The team judges AI a major contributor, while acknowledging uncertainty and alternative explanations. Anthropic redacted much of the evidence underlying the assessment. This new independent assessment goes beyond earlier Anthropic product announcements, while showing how limited public evidence complicates claims of AI accelerating AI research. Thinking Machines introduced Inkling 2 Small on 5 November, with 594 billion total parameters and 17 billion active per token. The model supports image inputs and is available for inference and fine-tuning through Tinker. Its weights remain closed, with an Apache 2.0 release planned for next week after external safety testing. This second model generation extends the earlier Inkling release, but self-hosting still depends on the promised weights becoming available. The Gemini API price for 720p video is US$0.07 per second, a 30% reduction from Omni 1.1. Google says the model is generally available through the Gemini API and Google Cloud, with multi-turn editing and stronger reference adherence. The new video API release adds longer clips at lower cost beyond Google’s previously covered models, reducing the expense of testing creative variants. Developers can choose Flare for speed or Sunburst for higher quality, with image markup and SVG exports also reaching the API. The company says low-quality Flare images can take as little as six seconds. This new visual-production release adds faster iteration and animation beyond OpenAI’s previously covered coding and cyber tools. This ongoing-work layer extends the earlier Perplexity Computer offering by keeping responsibilities active between individual requests. The current site lists a starting preorder price of US$399 and shipping in early 2027. It pairs with iPhone and Mac and claims up to 18 hours of battery life. items.body: Meta is rolling out specialized versions of its existing models , trained using its Muse Wonder series, to people who use Muse and Meta AI. They bring two Muse Wonder capabilities: Active Memory , which judges which earlier information still matters and which is stale, and Active Focus , which keeps working toward a goal when something goes wrong. Meta says the improved Muse models show a 2.4x reduction in forgetting information critical to a user's goal, and a 67% improvement in completing everyday tasks where unexpected issues arise. On its own Active Memory evaluation the current Muse model uses critical context correctly in 90% of tasks, against 76% for the previous one, and on Meta's Personal Superintelligence Index it scores 47% against 38%. Separately, Meta launched Spaces in Muse: a user describes an idea in chat and Muse builds a tracker, planner or project board in the sidebar, which can stay up to date from connected apps, TechCrunch reports. We summarize seven stories: the retreat in Anthropic's IPO valuation, OpenAI's funding, the second day of sharp declines in Asian markets, the Democratic Party's AI bill, the growing anti-data center movement in Europe, Nvidia chips being halted in Hong Kong, and Thinking Machines' new model. Table of Contents Sharp Braking for AI IPOs 1. Anthropic IPO: Valuation discussions retreat to $1.2–$1.3 trillion 2. OpenAI secures $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation 3. AI stock sell-off spreads to Asia on day two: Nikkei 225 down 6.1%, KOSPI temporarily halted 4. Democrats plan to introduce a series of AI bills starting in January 5. Anti-data center movement spreads to Europe; Google responds by 'generating its own power' 6. 600,000 of Nvidia's 'H200' chips stuck in Hong Kong 7. Thinking Machines releases new model 'Inkling 2 Small'; seeks to raise $5 billion at a $40 billion valuation Summary References 1. Anthropic IPO: Valuation discussions retreat to $1.2–$1.3 trillion On November 6, Bloomberg reported that investors considering purchasing shares in Anthropic's initial public offering (IPO) have begun discussing a valuation of $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion. Until recently, investors had been telling underwriters $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion. Since there was talk of up to $2 trillion in early October, this represents a significant drop in one month. Anthropic has been reported to be aiming for a listing in the week of November 16 and raising up to $100 billion. If realized, it would be the largest IPO in history. Formal investor presentations are expected to begin next week, but there is talk of plans to start with a smaller scale or the possibility of a delay. items.body: With the release of Patch 7.58, scheduled for Tuesday, November 10, 2026 , same-region player matching ─previously introduced to the Japan data center─will be implemented on the North American and European data centers. Matchmaking and party recruitment have thus far been limited to players on the same logical data center. However, with the introduction of same-region player matching, the scope will expand to cover all those on the same physical data center. This means that all players within the same physical data center will be eligible for matchmaking and party recruitment, regardless of their current world. Further information can be found below on the purpose and impact of same-region player matching. * The maintenance accompanying the release of Patch 7.58 is scheduled to last 24 hours. The maintenance schedule will be announced in the News once finalized. To better understand same-region player matching, it is useful to start with the structure of FFXIV's data centers. * See the current data center structure here . Physical Data Centers (Physical DC) The physical DCs (represented in blue on the diagram) are located in four regions : Japan, North America, Europe, and Oceania. The closer your place of residence is to the physical DC, the less likely you are to experience network lag; as such, players typically choose the physical DC located closest to their residence. Logical Data Centers (Logical DC) Each physical DC contains one to four logical DCs (represented in green on the diagram). Worlds Each logical DC contains five to eight Worlds (represented in gray on the diagram). Once same-region player matching is introduced in Patch 7.58, scheduled for Tuesday, November 10, 2026 , features that were restricted to the same logical DC will become usable across all logical DCs in the same physical DC (the same region). There will be no change to features only accessible on your Home World, or those that already operated across the same physical DC. Going forward, the rules for what can and cannot be carried out on a world in another logical DC will be the same as those currently in place for the World Visit system . View more information on the World Visit system here . The Data Center Travel system will no longer allow travel between logical DCs within North America, nor between logical DCs within Europe. However, it will still allow travel from the North American and European DCs to the Oceania DC. As cross-world linkshells, PvP Teams and Fellowships will be available regardless of current logical DC, they will be consolidated into a single…

items.body: Versions & Channels What's New in Dalamud v15 On this page What's New in Dalamud v15 Dalamud v15 is the current major version of Dalamud, and will release with Patch 7.5. This is a high-level overview of changes. You can see a code diff of all of these changes here . Dalamud.NET.Sdk Migration If you haven't done so yet, we strongly recommend migrating your plugin project to Dalamud.NET.Sdk . It includes the latest version of DalamudPackager, pinned to the current API level, and will make it easier for us to introduce changes to how we distribute SDK files in the future. We have added a new plugin base interface centered around asynchronous functions. This new interface is designed to reduce friction when needing to do async work during load and unload (foregoing the usage of patterns like Task.Run().GetAwaiter().GetResult() ), and encourage developers to not block the main thread unnecessarily, leading to hitches. It is currently still experimental, as it's somewhat fresh and not thoroughly tested, but the interface itself is stable. Plugins utilizing this interface fully initialize and uninitialize off the main thread. It offers a new Task LoadAsync(CancellationToken) function to accomplish this and inherits from IAsyncDisposable instead of IDisposable . The load task may be cancelled after a timeout, currently set at 60 seconds (may be changed later upon feedback), and the plugin is not considered loaded until this task completes successfully. Work that needs to be done on the main thread during load or dispose has to be shifted to the main thread through the IFramework interface (via IFramework.Run() , for example). Async disposal through IAsyncDisposable is not cancellable. The plugin must resolve this task and dispose its resources in a timely fashion. Remember to try out the LogMessage event introduced in API 14, which may be a suitable alternative for intercepting system messages. IEndObjects have been removed as they box the value and cause an impact on performance and allocation of memory building GC pressure. The change implements them as ref struct , which will prevent boxing and is in general less costly than a class, only Push... functions are still classes that can be taken across scope. using ( ImRaii . items.body: The 22-track collection captures Florence Welch and her band across their 2026 world tour, with the digital release available now and a triple-vinyl edition scheduled for March 2027. Florence + The Machine have released Everybody Scream Tour Live, a 22-track live album documenting the band’s 2026 world tour, with performances spanning North America, the UK and Europe. Available now digitally, Everybody Scream Tour Live brings together performances from the tour supporting Florence + The Machine’s latest studio era. A triple-vinyl edition is also available for pre-order ahead of its worldwide release on 19 March 2027. The collection captures the band during a series of major arena performances, including sold-out shows at New York’s Madison Square Garden and Barclays Center, alongside a two-night capacity run at Los Angeles’ Kia Forum. “Sympathy Magic (Live)” is the album’s focus track, showcasing the intensity of Florence Welch’s live performance. The 22-track set opens with the live version of the album’s title song, “Everybody Scream”, before moving through material from across the band’s catalogue. The selection balances songs from the current era with established favourites. “Witch Dance”, “Daffodil”, “Which Witch”, “You Can Have It All”, “Music By Men”, “Buckle”, “The Old Religion”, “One of the Greats” and “And Love” feature alongside familiar songs including “Shake It Out”, “Seven Devils”, “Cosmic Love”, “Spectrum (Say My Name)”, “King”, “Dog Days Are Over” and “Free”. The album also includes “Howl” and “Heaven Is Here”, while “Perfume and Milk” appears as a bonus track, bringing the total collection to 22 performances. Florence Welch established Florence + The Machine with the release of their debut album Lungs in 2009. The record introduced the band’s distinctive combination of alternative rock, orchestral arrangements and Welch’s powerful vocal performances, establishing an international audience. Subsequent albums Ceremonials (2011), How Big, How Blue, How Beautiful (2015), High As Hope (2018) and Dance Fever (2022) continued that progression, with each release expanding the band’s musical and lyrical scope. Everybody Scream Tour Live provides a broader document of the band’s concert performances, bringing together songs from different stages of their recording career in one collection. The digital album is available now on streaming and download platforms. The triple-vinyl edition is available to pre-order through the official Florence + The Machine webstore, with worldwide release scheduled for 19 March…

items.headline: Godzilla Minus Zero opens to about $31 million
items.summary: Toho's sequel took $14.7m on day one from 3,254 sites and scored an A on CinemaScore.
items.matters: only the fourth non-English film ever to top the US chart.
items.body: Toho/GKids’ “Godzilla Minus Zero” is off to a roaring start at the box office with a $14.7 million opening day at the box office, putting it on course for an industry estimated $31 million opening from 3,254 locations. That is nearly triple the $11.4 million that Takashi Yamazaki’s previous kaiju film, “Godzilla Minus One,” earned in December 2023 en route to a $57.4 million domestic total. “Minus Zero” is now just the fourth non-English film ever to take the No. 1 spot at the U.S. box office, joining “The Passion of the Christ,” the Zhang Yimou wuxia film “Hero,” and the anime film “Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle,” which was released by Crunchyroll last year in English and Japanese dubs. We will see if this sequel is able to exceed its predecessor’s total or if it proves to be more frontloaded with fans of “Minus One” simply rushing out faster to see it on opening weekend. But there are signs that “Minus Zero” may be in for a longer run as the movie not only has stellar scores with an A on CinemaScore and Rotten Tomatoes scores of 90% critics and 96% audience, but streaming guide site JustWatch reports that “Godzilla Minus One” has become the most watched film on streaming across all platforms this past week, showing a desire among uninitiated audiences to get caught up. In second is Warner Bros. Picture Animation’s “The Cat in the Hat” with a $6 million opening day from 4,003 locations as it is now tracking for an $18 million opening weekend. It’s an opening that’s below past Warner animated films like “DC League of Super Pets,” which launched to $23 million in the summer of 2022, and puts the Dr. Seuss adaptation on an uphill battle to avoid joining the long list of theatrical disappointments for Warner Bros. this year. The good news for “Cat in the Hat” is that it has enjoyed strong audience reception with an A on CinemaScore, with the highest marks coming from the core family demographic. The hope now for Warner Bros. is that this word-of-mouth allows the film to keep legging out with families all the way into and through Thanksgiving, building enough momentum with parents and kids to remain a popular offering amongst them even with Disney’s “Hexed” coming to theaters on Thanksgiving weekend. In a tight race for third is A24’s “You Can See Everything” and Sony Pictures’ “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” both with an industry estimated $8 million this weekend. For “You Can See Everything,” that’s a remarkable fourth weekend hold that makes it the only holdover in the top 5, bringing its total to $78.9 million through Sunday as it seeks to join…

items.headline: A second Cliff Booth trailer lands

items.matters: Regal and Cinemark are sitting it out, so AMC carries the US run.
items.body: Watch the high-octane new trailer for David Fincher’s Netflix movie 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth' arriving this Thanksgiving. Cliff Booth is back, and this time the trailer isn’t holding back on the language. Netflix has released the second trailer for David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth online, a red band cut that first played exclusively in front of the Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood IMAX re-release last weekend. When we broke down the 500+ IMAX locations confirmed for the film’s global release earlier this week, we noted that a special trailer was reportedly playing ahead of screenings of Tarantino’s 2019 film. That trailer is now available for everyone to see, and it’s easily the most revealing look at the plot we’ve had yet. It’s the second big theatrical tie-in for the film’s marketing campaign. The first official trailer back in September also debuted on the big screen first, playing in front of Resident Evil before Netflix put it online. Some of this will be familiar from September’s trailer, including Cliff’s dig at his old boss: the reason he stopped working with Rick Dalton is that Rick “got too fat for me to double him anymore.” Sorry, Leo. The highlight is the closing scene. When Charlie’s wife Toni (Carla Gugino) asks what the two men were “pow-wowing about,” Cliff improvises a pitch for a TV show about a famous actor and his stunt double, where “the dumbass actor gets involved with some Filipino gangsters and the stuntman has to get him out of it.” That’s the movie’s plot, in Cliff’s own words, played over a rapid-fire montage of car chases, gunfights, and a man crashing through an aquarium. Sony’s IMAX re-release of Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood returned to theaters on October 30th, a few weeks after Tarantino surprised the crowd at AFI Fest with the first 17 minutes of Cliff Booth following an IMAX screening of the original. Per Box Office Mojo, the re-release grossed $302,266 domestically across its opening weekend. That’s a modest number on limited IMAX-only screens, but anyone who bought a ticket also got the first look at this new trailer, which was arguably the point. Directed by David Fincher from a script by Quentin Tarantino, the film stars Brad Pitt alongside Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Peter Weller, Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis, Karren Karagulian, and Timothy Olyphant. items.headline: First AI Act harmonised standard is now citable
items.summary: EN 18286:2026 on quality management systems was referenced in the Official Journal via Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274.
items.matters: build to it and you get presumption of conformity with Article 17; skip it and you prove compliance yourself.
items.body: The European Commission has published the reference to the first harmonised standard supporting the implementation of the AI Act in the Official Journal of the European Union. The standard, EN 18286:2026 - Artificial intelligence - Quality management system for EU AI Act regulatory purposes , developed by CEN and CENELEC, provides a clear legal pathway for providers of high-risk AI systems to comply with the quality management system requirements under article 17 of the AI Act . Its publication through Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 means that providers implementing this standard will benefit from a presumption of conformity with the Article 17 requirements covered by the standard. EN 18286 translates these requirements into an operational quality management system (QMS). It is the only AI QMS standard with a presumption of conformity. It is mapped to Article 17 of the AI Act, built around the AI system lifecycle – rather than the organisation – and designed to be layered on top of the existing international standards – such as ISO/IEC 42001, ISO 9001 or a sectoral QMS (e.g. ISO 13485) – rather than replace them. EN 18286 explicitly allows providers in regulated sectors to integrate management systems, rather than run separate ones. Organisations without ISO/IEC 42001 that plan to place or put into service high-risk AI systems in the EU market can use EN 18286 to expand an existing QMS or build one that fulfills the requirements of article 17 requirements. The publication of this standard marks an important milestone in implementing the AI Act, ahead of the application of requirements for high-risk AI systems , with further harmonised standards expected to…

items.body: Welcome to this edition of the Dispatch from Brussels. After weeks of false starts, Member States have finally agreed their position on the Digital Omnibus, opening the way for negotiations with Parliament. On AI, the AI Office used the International AI Summit in Dublin to signal that AI Act enforcement against frontier model providers has begun, while Member States backed a new Dublin Declaration on trusted, safe and sovereign AI. Elsewhere, the Commission opened its first Digital Services Act investigation into Booking.com, telecoms ministers met in Limerick to discuss the Digital Networks Act, and the date of the UK–EU Summit has now been confirmed for 20 November. Below is a more detailed overview of what has kept the EU tech policy space busy. UK–EU Summit confirmed for 20 November : On 12 October, the Council confirmed that the second UK–EU Summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November, where António Costa and Ursula von der Leyen will welcome Prime Minister Andy Burnham. The published agenda covers defence and security, energy, agrifood, climate, people-to-people contacts, and migration and law enforcement, with leaders expected to adopt a joint declaration. techUK will make a strong case in favour of discussing key tech issues at the summit and will update members on any potential industry engagement opportunities. Council finally agrees its position on the Digital Omnibus : On 21 October, EU ambassadors agreed the Council’s negotiating mandate on the Digital Omnibus, the Commission’s package amending the GDPR, ePrivacy rules and the EU’s data rules to simplify the digital rulebook (see our previous update on the postponed 7 October vote). The deal was unlocked by a final compromise from the Irish Presidency strengthening protection for trade secrets linked to industrial know-how, the issue that had pushed Germany and France block earlier attempts. Under the Council’s text, trade secrets would only have to be shared once confidentiality measures are in place. Incident reporting: the Council rejected the Commission’s proposed single EU-wide reporting entry point, favouring national entry points, an EU-level information point and more harmonised notification rules. Data: consolidated rules on data altruism and data intermediation, and the possibility for public bodies to charge gatekeepers higher fees for re-using public-sector data. Inter-institutional negotiations can begin once the European Parliament has adopted its own position. Leaders at the European Council of 15–16 October also called on co-legislators to finalise the simplification…

items.body: On 28 October the EDPS published its FAQs on personal data breach notification. Risk assessment should start as soon as the controller knows, with a reasonable degree of certainty, that a breach has occurred, and should be carried out for each combination of processing operation and category of data subjects. Phased notifications must use the dedicated form: informal email updates are not accepted. A processor may notify the EDPS if its arrangements with the controller allow it, but responsibility remains with the controller. The FAQs also cover mitigation measures and communication to data subjects. On 29 October the EDPS reported on Opinion 27/2026, dated 27 October, on the framework agreement proposed by the Commission on 10 September. The agreement would govern the reciprocal exchange of information between Member State and US authorities for border checks, travel authorizations and visas, allowing identity verification, screening and vetting of travelers. The United States requires Visa Waiver Program partners to conclude an Enhanced Border Security Partnership by the end of 2026, which is why the Commission proposes provisional application of the agreement. According to Wojciech Wiewiórowski, this would be the first time the EU has shared personal data, including biometrics, with a third country on this scale for border control. The recommendations concern the selection of the national systems to draw on, the listing of relevant offenses in the bilateral agreements, a concrete definition of the link between the traveler and the State, and an objective, case-by-case link between the person and the risk. The EDPS also asks the Commission to verify that judicial redress is available in practice regardless of nationality, and calls for the United States to be required to notify the EU, before provisional application, of the supervisory authorities it designates, with their tasks and powers. In a post published on 26 October, Wojciech Wiewiórowski looks back on the fourth meeting of the AI Act Correspondents Network, held on 6 October at the European Parliament’s premises in Brussels with correspondents from the 78 EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. The topics were the Article 50 transparency obligations, most of which now apply, the EDPS Compass 2026–2027 and the pilot AI regulatory sandbox under Article 57(3) of the AI Act. The EDPS now also acts as market surveillance authority for AI systems used by the EU institutions. The network meets again on 23 February 2027. items.headline: The sea's grip on the global economy
items.summary: El País on the five chokepoints that decide what the world pays for everything: Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb, Suez, Panama and Malacca, and why a strait twenty miles wide can move inflation on three continents.
items.body: More than 80% of global merchandise trade is transported by sea, a vast share that, in times of peace, allows commerce to flow smoothly but, in times of turmoil, starkly reveals the oceans’ influence over the economy and consumers’ purchasing power. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway just over 20 miles wide through which 20% of the world’s oil consumption passed as recently as February, is a traumatic and unprecedented example of how disrupting maritime traffic through a strategic chokepoint can trigger a massive snowball effect. Less energy supply, a sudden spike in fuel prices, soaring shipping costs and higher inflation. It is impossible for the global economy to function independently of the sea. The shockwave from the closure of Hormuz has been global and has hit the U.S. economy particularly hard. U.S. President Donald Trump likely never imagined that the conflict launched alongside Israel against Iran would last this long, or that it would drive gasoline and diesel prices for Americans to record highs. The collapse in maritime traffic through Hormuz has disrupted oil exports from the Persian Gulf and sharply increased transportation costs worldwide. According to analysts, higher shipping rates are adding more than $30 to the cost of each barrel of oil, roughly 10 times more than before the conflict. Hormuz, with its enormous influence over the world’s energy supply, is the clearest example of the strategic importance of maritime straits to global trade and the economy. But the world is dotted with other waterways that are just as critical to the movement of goods and the shape of the geopolitical landscape. These are the so-called chokepoints: highly sensitive passages through which a significant share of global trade flows. Whoever controls them holds a lever capable of moving the world. For weather-related rather than military reasons, the Panama Canal is another hotspot. Drought linked to the El Niño phenomenon has forced the Panama Canal Authority to cut traffic and impose draft restrictions on vessels, as the canal’s locks require large volumes of water to operate. The risk of disruption has also briefly hovered over the Strait of Malacca, located between Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia, which is one of the world’s busiest shipping routes, serving as the main corridor between Asia and Europe via the Indian Ocean.
